sections.heading: 1. Understanding Poverty
points: **Poverty** = the inability to meet the **basic needs** of life — food, clothing, shelter, education, health.
Indicators: **landlessness, illiteracy, poor health, hunger, lack of basic amenities**.
**Social exclusion** and **vulnerability** are aspects of poverty.

sections.heading: 2. The Poverty Line
points: The **poverty line** = a minimum level of income (or consumption) needed to meet basic needs; those below it are 'poor'.
It is based on a minimum **calorie intake** (about **2400 calories/day in rural** and **2100 in urban** areas) and a minimum expenditure.
The **poverty ratio (head count ratio)** = the % of people below the poverty line; it has **declined** over the decades.

sections.heading: 3. Vulnerable Groups and Disparities
points: Most affected: **Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes**, **rural agricultural labourers** and **urban casual labourers**.
**Inter-state disparity:** poverty is higher in states like **Bihar, Odisha, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh**; lower in **Kerala, Punjab, Himachal Pradesh**.
Even within families, women, children and the elderly may be poorer.

sections.heading: 4. Causes and Anti-Poverty Measures
points: **Causes:** low economic growth (colonial legacy), high population, unemployment, unequal land distribution, indebtedness, social factors.

sub: **Targeted anti-poverty programmes:** **MGNREGA (2005)** (100 days of wage employment), **PMGSY, NRLM, PMAY, National Food for Work**, etc.

points: Goal: reduce poverty and provide a **dignified life** for all.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Poverty = inability to meet basic needs; aspects: social exclusion + vulnerability.
Poverty line = minimum income/consumption; ~2400 (rural) / 2100 (urban) calories/day.
Poverty ratio (head count ratio) = % below the poverty line (declining).
Most vulnerable: SC/ST, rural agricultural & urban casual labourers.
Anti-poverty: economic growth + programmes (MGNREGA 2005 = 100 days work).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: The **poverty line** uses a minimum **calorie** requirement (higher in rural: ~2400 vs ~2100 urban).
The **poverty ratio (head count ratio)** = **percentage** below the poverty line.
**MGNREGA (2005)** guarantees **100 days** of wage employment.
Poverty is **higher** in Bihar/Odisha/MP and **lower** in Kerala/Punjab.
